Adaptive spatial blocking for B-KAMP

bkamp_block.Rd

Partition a marked pattern into rectangular blocks using grid representation, two block identification phases, and block complement.

Usage

bkamp_block(
  ppp_obj,
  univariate = TRUE,
  mark1,
  mark2 = NULL,
  split_max = NULL,
  n_min = NULL,
  rho1 = NULL,
  rho2 = Inf,
  max_grid_dim = 100L
)

Arguments

ppp_obj

A marked ppp with a rectangular observation window.

univariate

Logical; TRUE for one target type, FALSE for two.

mark1

Variable used to mark the points in the point pattern object for the first type.

mark2

Variable used to mark the points in the point pattern object for the second type (optional, only used if univariate is FALSE).

split_max

Maximum point count per initial grid cell. NULL uses sqrt(n), where n denotes the total number of points in ppp_obj.

n_min

Minimum target/background counts, or type1/type2/background counts. NULL uses the paper's square-root thresholds based on full-pattern counts.

rho1

Phase I bound on longer/shorter side ratio. NULL uses the full-window ratio.

rho2

Phase II aspect ratio bound. Defaults to Inf; must be >= rho1.

max_grid_dim

Maximum number of grid cells per axis to search. Defaults to 100.

Value

A list whose elements are marked ppp blocks.

Details

Adaptive spatial blocking

Note

The observation window must be rectangular. Returned blocks retain their original marks. Unassigned points are excluded with a warning.

Examples

# one image from the ovarian cancer data in the package
ids <- unique(ovarian_df$sample_id)
img <- ovarian_df[ovarian_df$sample_id == ids[4], ]
pp <- spatstat.geom::ppp(img$x, img$y,
                         window = spatstat.geom::owin(range(img$x), range(img$y)),
                         marks = img$immune)

blocks <- bkamp_block(pp, mark1 = "immune")
length(blocks)
#> [1] 21
